Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities
Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request
a disability-related modification or accommodation.

The Investment Policy Advisory Committee welcomes and encourages public participation at the
Investment Policy Advisory Committee meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of
business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3)
minutes or as specified by the Chairperson. Anyone wishing to address the Investment Policy
Advisory Committee is requested to fill out a speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the
Chambers. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of Investment Policy
Advisory Committee minute preparation.

The Investment Policy Advisory Committee is a new committee, effective July 1, 2017. With the
City Treasurer, the Committee shall be responsible for recommending investment brokers,
proposing changes to investment policy and practices, presenting investment reports, and evaluating
and recommending banking-related matters. Meetings are to review, discuss and develop
recommendation on matters such as investment and banking vendors, policy, transactions, returns
and performance, brokers, and strategy.

The Investment Policy Advisory Committee, at the direction of the Chairman with concurrence of
the Committee, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  VICTORIA A. LOZZI, CITY TREASURER /s/
  JOHN DOWNS, FINANCE DIRECTOR /s/

SUBJECT: QUARTERLY INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 30, 2017

DATE:  JULY 25, 2017

ISSUE

Shall the City Council accept the quarterly investment portfolio report as of June 30, 2017
representing the fourth quarter of fiscal year (FY) 2016-17?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

The City’s investment policy calls for a quarterly reporting on the status of the investment portfolio.
This performance report is provided for public disclosure and accountability in this important area
of fiscal stewardship.

The quarterly report is prepared in coordination between the City Treasurer and Finance Director to
present the following:
  • A status update on the condition of the portfolio,
  • A listing of all securities held in trust by Union Bank, and
  • A display of the current investment asset mix including all cash balances.

The quarter-end investment portfolio reports are posted and maintained on the City’s website
(www.pvestates.org) for the general public under meetings and agendas within the July 25, 2017
agenda.

DISCUSSION

As of June 30, 2017, yields are very similar to the prior quarter and remain at the lower end of a 10
year historic spectrum. The City’s yield for its Federal Obligations and Certificates of Deposits
(CDs) is 1.68% (1.72% the past quarter). On a cost basis of $12,375,000 (market value $12,268,359)

  Page 1 of 3

  001
 estimated annual income at the current yield is $206,542. The bank-liquid cash account of
$7,788,766 held by the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF), at an interest rate of 0.92% (0.78%
Prior Quarter). This is the highest rate the State has earned on the Pooled Money Investment
Account (PMIA) since March 2009. The current yield will approximate $71,656 in annualized
earnings, for total estimated annual income of $278,198. The City’s money remains secure and
cannot be accessed by the State or the federal government.

The City’s June 2017 investment account statement, provided by our custodian – Union Bank
(redacted & attached), shows a market value of $12,268,359 and an unrealized loss of ($106,641).
Since the City typically holds its investments to maturity, full-face (par) value is received, and no
realized gain/(loss) of funds is expected.

Investments have maturity dates ranging from 2017 to 2022. The City experienced zero maturities
and one redemption in the quarter. Income on LAIF balances, varies as amounts are deposited and
withdrawn (for operations) on a continual basis. The returns on our Federal obligation securities and
CDs are fixed unless liquidated by us or the Federal obligations are called (early redemption) by the
Fed.

As previously stated, the City’s authority to invest and reinvest City funds is derived from City
Council Policy. The City Treasurer and/or his/her designee, has been delegated the responsibility to
manage the City’s investments. The City abides by the “Prudent Person” rule, per the Civil Code
section 2261.

The City Council has been provided with all the major and necessary information, to give assurance
that the City’s investments are being managed properly. More specific information is available (from
independent brokers), including graphs, pie charts, etc. for an additional cost to the City. Also
attached the June 2017 redacted account statement from Union Bank which includes a complete
asset detail of our portfolio.

For the third time in four months, the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by .25% at
their June 2017 meeting. The unemployment rate declined to 4.3%, and the financial equity markets
have paused, after a steady after rise from the November Presidential election. Regardless, the
current level of investments can accommodate cash needs, and can support additional investments
as we remain ever attentive to changing trends in the marketplace/economy.

CERTIFICATIONS

As Treasurer for the City of Palos Verdes Estates, I certify that the investments of the City comply
with the City’s current Investment Policy. Furthermore, I certify that the City is able to meet its
expenditure requirements for the next six months.

___________________________________

Victoria, A. Lozzi, City Treasurer

  County Investment Pool as an investment option within the City’s investment policy.

  2017-18 investment report format for discussion and review at the September 6, 2017
  Investment Policy Advisory Committee meeting.

  Actions taken by this Committee are advisory.
  The City Council will take action on all appropriate items on September 12, 2017.
 5. Review bank service fees.

  No action taken. Committee provided direction to staff to consider topic in future
  discussions regarding issue of annual total cost of Service Fees as well reviewing Union
  Banks Custody Fees and Custody agreement.

6. Discuss cash flow analysis

  Investment Policy Advisory Committee Chair Member Lozzi recommended and approved
  by Committee Member Ying,(2nd by Committee Member Sagolla) to provide month to

  meeting with Committee Chair Lozzi, Finance Director Downs and Union Bank

7. Identify topics for discussion at future meetings.

  Investment Policy Advisory Committee Chair Member Lozzi recommended and approved
  by Committee Member Ying,(2nd by Committee Member Sagolla) to discuss draft
